title: GSMA Innovation Forum in Hangzhou Explores How AI Is Becoming Embedded Across Devices, Robots and Industry
snippet: As AI moves into its next phase, the GSMA showcases resources on connected embodied intelligence, industrial AI deployment and operator use cases 26 November 2026, Hangzhou: The GSMA brought together mobile operators, policymakers and technology companies at its 2026 Innovation Forum today to examine what it takes to deploy AI at scale across connected devices, […] The post GSMA Innovation Forum in Hangzhou Explores How AI Is Becoming Embedded Across Devices, Robots and Industry appeared first on Newsroom.
fullText:
As AI moves into its next phase, the GSMA showcases resources on connected embodied intelligence, industrial AI deployment and operator use cases

26 November 2026, Hangzhou: The GSMA brought together mobile operators, policymakers and technology companies at its 2026 Innovation Forum today to examine what it takes to deploy AI at scale across connected devices, robotics and industrial operations.

Participants shared lessons from deployments in China and other markets, focusing on which AI tasks can run on devices, when cloud computing is needed and what mobile networks must support as deployments expand. The forum also gave operators and technology companies from China and around the world an opportunity to explore how they could work together on these challenges.

The GSMA showcased three industry resources covering how intelligent machines ca

n combine on-device and cloud-based AI, the connectivity and computing infrastructure needed to deploy physical AI at scale, and examples of how mobile operators are helping businesses use AI across sectors.

Sihan Bo Chen, Head of Greater China, GSMA, said: “AI is rapidly moving beyond individual applications and becoming embedded across devices, networks and industries. At this year’s Innovation Forum, we’re bringing together leaders from across the mobile and technology ecosystem to explore how connectivity can accelerate this transition, from enabling the next generation of AI-powered devices and connected embodied intelligence to supporting industrial AI deployment. Realising these opportunities requires collaboration across the ecosystem, and China’s innovation landscape provides valuable insights into how AI can be applied at scale across industries. This week discussions take place ahead of MWC27 Shanghai, where the GSMA looks forward to bringing together leaders from across connectivity, AI and 6G to turn this ambition into action.”

The forum featured keynote addresses from Gao Tongqing, Chairman of GTI; Vivian Jiang, Chair of Deloitte China; and Ian Shih, President of Rockwell Automation China. Three panel discussions brought together senior representatives from leading organisations including China Mobile, China Unicom, Huawei, ZTE, HONOR, Alibaba Cloud, AI100, Unitree Robotics, Gamma Robotics, Neusoft, DingTalk and the Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine, AILINK, smart Software among others.

What it takes to deploy AI across devices and industries

Three executive-led panel discussions  explored how connectivity can support AI in different settings.

AI-powered devices. Kevin Pang, Head of Strategic Engagement, Greater China, GSMA, explored the transformations brought to the end-device ecosystem by AI, the development opportunities for AI-native smartphones, and the collaborative ecosystem and standardisation efforts required to achieve the large-scale implementation of autonomous, cross-application AI agents.

Connected embodied intelligence. Hong Liu, Head of Technology GSMA, led a discussion on how robotics and other intelligent machines can combine on-device processing with cloud-based AI, and what these applications could require from future mobile networks.

Industrial AI. Lin Li, Head of Ecosystem Engagement, GSMA, chaired a discussion focusing on the integrated application of AI and intelligent connectivity across sectors such as manufacturing, automotive, healthcare, and education, explored how to advance AI from isolated innovations toward core business scenarios and achieve large-scale implementation.

The resources showcased at the forum were:

Connected Embodied Intelligence: A Key Path to Real-World Deployment

The Path to Industrial Physical AI at Scale: Connectivity, Computing and Ecosystem Collaboration

Operator Best Practices: AI Empowering Verticals Use Cases 2026

GSMA recognises China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom for eSIM contributions

At the event’s eSIM Forum, the GSMA presented three awards recognising contributions to the development of China’s eSIM ecosystem.

China eSIM Ecosystem Outstanding – Contribution Award – China Mobile

China eSIM Ecosystem Innovation Leadership Award – China Telecom

China eSIM Ecosystem Pioneer Award – China Unicom

-ENDS-

About GSMA

The GSMA is a global organisation unifying the mobile ecosystem to discover, develop and deliver innovation foundational to positive business environments and societal change. Our vision is to unlock the full power of connectivity so that people, industry, and society thrive. Representing mobile operators and organisations across the mobile ecosystem and adjacent industries, the GSMA delivers for its members across three broad pillars: Connectivity for Good, Industry Services and Solutions, and Outreach. This activity includes advancing policy, tackling today’s biggest societal challenges, underpinning the technology and interoperability that make mobile work, and providing the world’s largest platform to convene the mobile ecosystem at the MWC and M360 series of events.

We invite you to find out more at gsma.com
